title: Putting It All Together: Custom Error Responses
description: Create a consistent error response structure and combine validation with global handling.

slides.title: Design a Consistent Error Response 🎨

quizData.question: Why should you return a structured error response instead of a simple string?

options.text: It's required by the HTTP spec
It provides consistency and makes it easier for clients to handle errors
It prevents the application from crashing

quizData.explanation: A consistent error structure helps clients programmatically handle different error scenarios.

slides.title: Test Your Error Handling 🧪
slides.content:
# Try It Out!

1. Send a GET request to a non‑existent resource → 404 with custom response.
2. Send a POST with invalid data (e.g., email missing) → 400 with field‑specific messages.
3. Cause an unexpected exception (e.g., null pointer) → 500 with sanitized message (and logged stack trace).

Your API now handles errors gracefully and consistently.

slides.title: Don't Forget to Log! 📝
slides.content: Always log the full stack trace of unexpected exceptions. This helps you debug issues without exposing sensitive details to clients.
